lens: Spotify-style persona library: shelves, carousels, cover art per persona, made-for-you scenario mixes
name: Shelf & Coach Studio
one_liner: A Spotify-style studio of persona shelves and cover art, with a live coach rail that whispers cues and scores the rubric while the call runs.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the shelf lens: horizontal persona carousels, cover art per persona, made-for-you mixes. Changed two things. The live call uses a Voicenotes-style coach rail instead of a music-player layout, because a call needs a coach, not a queue. The debrief uses evidence cards, not shelves. Mobbin returned no Spotify screen, so SoundCloud and Meetup stand in. Firecrawl was rate-limited, so competitor and library research used WebSearch. Self-scores (1-10): A look 8, B UX 7, C unique 7, D coaching 6 (reaches 5.1+ only with measured cue latency), E persona library 8, F1 SaaS 6, F2 selling to entities 6, F3 not worth it 4.

design_language.typography: Geist Sans 600 for headings with -0.02em tracking (40px desktop H1, 28px mobile). Geist Mono for scores, timers and tabular numerals. Body 15px over 1.55 line height. Replaces Sora and Inter.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 14px card radius, 12px cover-art radius, 999px pills. Depth comes from tonal surfaces and 1px line borders, not shadows. Cover art gets a faint 1px inner highlight.
design_language.motion: Shelves use CSS scroll-snap with Motion arrow nudges. Cue cards slide up over 200ms and fade after 12s. Score meters tween over 600ms. Waveform runs at 30fps. All motion turns off under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react line icons at 20px with 1.75 stroke. Persona role glyphs are a custom 24px set on a 2px grid. No emoji in UI chrome.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default. Light mode uses the same token names with canvas #F6F7F9 and surface #FFFFFF, switched by data-theme and prefers-color-scheme. Every color is a token on :root, so the redesign ships in both modes.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Architecture: the persona runs on the OpenAI Realtime API with its context isolated, so it never sees coaching. A separate coach model reads the same transcript events and emits typed cues: next-best question, talk-track step, objection alert, and a pace or filler nudge. At most one whisper per 20 seconds. Target: a cue visible within 1.5 seconds of the rep finishing a turn, to be measured, not promised. Rubric meters update after each rep turn using the same evidence rules as the debrief, so live and final scores agree. The coach setting (Quiet, Balanced, Intense) is user-controlled, and text mode gets the same coach. Strong-reply lines stay locked until the debrief, so practice still builds the skill.
persona_library_and_wizard: Launch target: about 120 personas across 12 industries (home services, insurance, mortgage, solar, auto, medical devices, SaaS SDR and AE, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections). Each persona has a role, difficulty, objection tags and cover art, and facets filter the shelves live. 'Daily Mix' is made-for-you: it blends personas that target the user's weakest criteria. The AI wizard takes a job description, product URL, CRM note, ICP or pasted call, and outputs a persona, opening line, weighted rubric and scripted objection replies, with each field source-cited. Every output passes a schema check before save and exports as YAML for a pull request.
signature_moments: Lyrics-style transcript: the current line glows as the rep speaks, like synced lyrics.
Objection alert drops in as a coral card the moment the persona raises price, timing or a competitor.
Daily Mix: 'Pricing objections, week 42' built from the rep's weakest rubric line.
Debrief quote chips that jump the replay to the exact second of the quote.
A minimized call keeps a mini-player with timer and coach pill on every page.
openai_fund_angle: OpenAI is visible, not buried. The call footer reads 'Voice: OpenAI Realtime', and a model inspector drawer lists the model behind the persona, the coach and the grader, with tokens and cost per call, so reviewers see credit use directly. The wizard drafts personas and rubrics with GPT, and cover art comes from an OpenAI image model at build time. Contributors are invited in: a /contribute page with a 'good first persona' board, a published YAML schema, and an 'Open PR' button in the wizard. CI validates persona files and rubric weights, a loop Codex (CLI or Codex for Open Source PR review) can run on every pull request. The landing page shows a contributor wall of real persona authors.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1: move Tailwind 3 to 4, map current tokens to the new palette behind the existing class names, and ship the landing page and persona shelves. Phase 2: the coach rail, cue pipeline and live rubric meters, behind a feature flag, with latency measured. Phase 3: the debrief evidence layout, the wizard, the progress dashboard and the team view. Voice, text, grading, Prisma data and accounts stay untouched. Retire the blurry orb from the call screen in phase 2.

risks: HeroUI license is reported as MIT in official docs but Apache-2.0 in another index. Verify the LICENSE file before adoption; fallback is shadcn/ui (copy-in components on Radix or Base UI).
The Tailwind 3 to 4 migration touches every screen and the custom classes in globals.css. It needs screenshot regression tests before merge.
A second model stream for coaching adds token cost on every call. Cap cue frequency and show the cost in the model inspector.
Cue latency under 1.5 seconds is unproven, especially on mobile networks. Measure it before claiming a score above 5.1 on the coaching criterion.
Per-persona cover art has generation cost and licensing questions. Keep a deterministic gradient fallback and pre-render covers at build time.
Library size depends on content contributors. If the 120-persona target slips, launch with a curated 40 across the highest-volume industries.
Competitor claims (Hyperbound, Second Nature, Yoodli) come from vendor-authored blogs. Verify before any pitch or landing-page comparison.
